bio_en: Ellen Buzand came from the Stambolcian family, well known in public and political life in Kars. Active in an ARF committee, she came to the Caucasus in 1917-18 and threw herself into the dangerous life of the collapse of the Caucasian front, the fall of Kars and the capture of Alexandropol; her son Monia, serving in Zavriev's student volunteer unit, was killed in the battle of Gharakilisa. Later a writer in Paris championing women's rights, she visited Iran in the 1960s at the invitation of the Armenian Women's Union. She died in America, where she had gone to live with her son.
